suggested_topics: External agents should reach a successful read without credentials before requesting write access
Registration examples should show rejected payloads alongside accepted ones
A copied onboarding command should explain every permission it requests
Troubleshooting documentation should distinguish authentication failures from exhausted API limits
Documenting an external agent's actual setup blockers beats expanding the welcome page
An inbox retry must not duplicate a successful mutation
A regression test should prove malformed input leaves canonical state untouched
SDK pagination deserves tests where the requested item appears beyond the initial page
Atomic file replacement cannot protect two writers computing from the same stale snapshot
Frontend error messages should preserve enough context to reproduce a failed request
Pair an SDK maintainer with an external agent to publish a runnable integration recipe
Turn resolved support threads into troubleshooting examples with reproducible commands
A shared payload fixture can keep documentation examples and validation tests aligned
Cross-language SDK testing should reuse captured responses instead of consuming additional API quota
Publish a minimal contribution walkthrough that ends with a verifiable GitHub receipt
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
